svg.text: Project profile — the one file everything else refers to
Ten keys, two clusters, one registry. Change a value here and every skill, hook, and manifest follows.
.kiro/steering/project-profile.md · inclusion: always — loads on every single turn
small enough to justify loading every turn
Values that vary per environment. Every other file in .kiro/ refers to these keys instead of hard-coding a name.
When a skill or steering file writes <app>, <cluster>, or <owner>, the value is substituted from here.
If a value is still a placeholder, ask the user for it before generating files. Guessing here propagates into every app.
colour banding groups them by what they govern
Argo CD AppProject for generated Applications
Value written to metadata.labels.owner — Gatekeeper requires it on every Namespace
spec.timeZone for CronJobs — the scheduled-job archetype default
Region for both clusters and all app resources
EKS Auto Mode — see the constraints this implies in stage 8
Per-app IAM, declared in each app's iam.tf — see stage 8
Switchable: gatekeeper or none — none skips every policy check but the Kustomize builds
Ingress controller class — the WAFv2 constraint only matches internet-facing ALB Ingress
use these exact values wherever an account ID is needed — never a bare <account>
Hosts the ECR registry; verified first
Pulls from dev's ECR; promoted to
Both account IDs are placeholders from the AWS documentation convention.
Replace both with real values in one pass — they appear in every app's iam.tf, not just in this file.
the source registry never reaches a manifest
Every app image lives in a single ECR registry in the dev account, with a repository policy granting 444455556666 pull access.
The repository is created elsewhere — assume it exists, named after the app. Source may be Docker Hub, GHCR, or a local build; that is only the input.
One registry means promoting to prod is promoting a digest — no cross-account copy that could change the bytes.
no sibling platform repo, no external Terraform repo — do not reference one
Everything an app needs lives here: manifests, cluster configuration, and the IAM that grants it AWS access.
iam.tf # IAM policy + Pod Identity association
bootstrap/ # Argo CD install and root manifests per cluster
no app deploys from base alone; none ships to one cluster
An app is complete only when all three exist:
Promotion is a change to the prod overlay — usually a newer image digest — not the creation of a prod overlay that did not exist.
Creating prod at promotion time means the first prod deploy is also the first time that overlay was ever built,
which is exactly when you discover the missing value.
Each app declares its own IAM
apps/<app>/iam.tf holds the app's IAM policy and its EKS Pod Identity association for both clusters. Nothing else.
The exact shape lives in the identity and secrets steering file — and because identity is per-app, an over-broad role is a per-app review question, not a platform default.
three keys above quietly decide what you must not scaffold
The AWS Load Balancer Controller, EBS CSI driver, and node lifecycle are all managed by EKS Auto Mode.
The ServiceAccount needs no IAM annotation — the association itself is the binding.
So manifests stay free of account IDs and role ARNs entirely.
Require Namespace labels.owner and CPU and memory requests/limits on every container — including init containers and sidecars.
Run local gator checks against the in-repo bundle: policies/base with per-cluster overlays at policies/overlays/<cluster>.
Setting this key to none skips every policy check except the Kustomize builds.
one always-on file → ten keys → two clusters → one registry → every manifest downstream
